newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index hits record highs, value eases.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index hits record highs, value eases.

text.p: Kuwait's share index finished the week to Wednesday at a record high while trade value eased with dealers focusing on stocks they expect to pay high year-end dividend.
"People are buying blue chips. The market is after a high dividend," said dealer Mohammad al-Duhaishi. "And there are shares that are expected to double their mid-year prices," he added.
"Selective trade means higher prices and less deals. If you want to get good shares you pay more," said another dealer.
The index rose 76.3 points or four percent to 1,954.2 points from 1,877.9 points. Gainers led losers 41-10, while six remained unchanged.

The total value of traded shares fell 13.5 percent to 285.5 million dinars ($995 million) -- a daily average of 57.1 million. Volume eased 19.2 percent to 965 million shares, a daily average of 193 million shares.
The exchange operates for two and a half hours five days a week.
Dealers attributed the upward trend to capital flows from neighbouring states, strong mid-year results by listed firms, lack of other local investment vehicles and strong economic indicators.

Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds run by local firms.
Kuwait is considering opening trade to foreign investors.
Commercial Bank, Investment Projects, United Realty, National Industries and Gulf Bank were among the most actively traded shares.

Banks dominated trade in terms of value with 33 percent, followed by investment firms with 20.4 percent and industrials with 15.3 percent. Investment firms were the most active by volume with 25.7 percent.
